tone_statements.citation: Ahland, Colleen. 2016. Daatsʼíin, a newly identified undocumented language of western Ethiopia: A preliminary examination. In Doris L. Payne, Sara Pacchiarotti & Mokaya Bosire (eds.), Diversity in African languages, 417-449. Berlin: Language Science Press. DOI 10.17169/langsci.b121.493
tone_statements.quote: Daatsʼíin has two tones, high (H) and low (L), as represented in the near minimal pairs in (6) and (7). H tone is indicated with a accute mark ˊ over the vowel, L tone is unmarked, and a HL sequence on a single vowel is indicated with a haceck ̂ over the vowel. Preliminary analysis suggests that Daatsʼíin also exhibits downstepped H tones. For example, the final L tone of the HL pattern on intransitive (S) bound pronominals (Table 4 in §4.2) induces a downstepped H tone on a following H-initial morpheme (see Table 5 in §4.2). (6) LL /giʃa/ 'stone(s)' HH /gíʃí/ 'see'

tone.says: Sec. 3.3 Tone: two tones, H and L (H marked with acute, L unmarked, HL on one vowel with circumflex), near-minimal pairs given; preliminary evidence of downstepped H, e.g. the final L of the HL melody on intransitive (S) bound pronominals downsteps a following H-initial morpheme; sec. 4.2 adds that S vs A bound pronominals differ in tonal melody (H(L) vs L), i.e. tone also has grammatical load.

sources.note: Citation context only: Ahland 2016 fn. 15 and sec. 11 cite Kelly 2014 for tone variation on free pronouns that may indicate a split alignment system (1st person ergative-absolutive vs 3rd person nominative-accusative), evidence 'inconclusive'; the paper treats alignment, which in Daats'iin is marked by tonal melody on bound pronominals (S = H(L), A = L), so it bears on grammatical tone rather than the tone inventory.
